Overview of equations and their usefulness
Converting word problems to mathematical models

bullet_points.text: Pairs of Linear Equations in Two Variables
Explore how two unknown quantities are represented
Learn methods to solve these equations

visual_content.verbatim_text: In mathematics and in real life, many situations involve two unknown quantities that depend on each other simultaneously. For example, when we buy two different items together, calculate ages of two people, or determine distance and speed, we are often dealing with two variables connected by two conditions. To represent such situations mathematically, we use pair of linear equations in two variables.

bullet_points.text: Clear overview of what equations are
Each equation represents a straight line

visual_content.verbatim_text: A linear equation in two variables represents a straight line when drawn on a graph. When two such equations describe the same situation, their common solution gives values of the variables that satisfy both equations at the same time. This makes the chapter extremely important because it helps convert real-life word problems into mathematical equations and then solve them systematically.
